content.text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents and a piperazine ring.

- **Benzene ring:** The CF3 group sits at the top left, on the carbon at the far left of the ring. The NO2 group is on the upper right carbon. The piperazine nitrogen is attached to the lower right carbon.
- **Substituent positions:** Taking the piperazine-bearing carbon as C1, the NO2 carbon is C2 (adjacent). Going around the ring, the next carbon is C3 (the top vertex, a CH), and the CF3 carbon is C4. So the CF3 is para to the piperazine, which fits the ring geometry.
- **Piperazine:** The nitrogen attached to the ring is linked through two CH2 groups on each side to an NH, forming a six-membered ring.

This is 1-(2-nitro-4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)piperazine.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)c1ccc(N2CCNCC2)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1
